title: GMAT Practice

bank.question: During an MBA admissions team review, 16 applications are marked urgent, representing 20 per cent of the total. How many applications are in the full list?
bank.explanation: If 20 per cent of the total equals 16, the total is 16 divided by 0.20, which is 80.

bank.question: In a graduate finance class review, 48 interview slots are marked urgent, representing 40 per cent of the total. How many interview slots are in the full list?
bank.explanation: If 40 per cent of the total equals 48, the total is 48 divided by 0.40, which is 120.

bank.question: For an executive education office review, 90 practice sets are marked urgent, representing 30 per cent of the total. How many practice sets are in the full list?
bank.explanation: If 30 per cent of the total equals 90, the total is 90 divided by 0.30, which is 300.

bank.question: At a business school cohort review, 45 case packs are marked urgent, representing 25 per cent of the total. How many case packs are in the full list?
bank.explanation: If 25 per cent of the total equals 45, the total is 45 divided by 0.25, which is 180.

bank.question: As 120 study cards are arranged into equal groups of 5, how many cards are left over?
bank.explanation: Dividing 120 by 5 gives a quotient of 24 with a remainder of 0, so 0 cards are left over.

bank.question: While 105 study cards are arranged into equal groups of 11, how many cards are left over?
bank.explanation: Dividing 105 by 11 gives a quotient of 9 with a remainder of 6, so 6 cards are left over.

bank.question: When 132 study cards are arranged into equal groups of 7, how many cards are left over?
bank.explanation: Dividing 132 by 7 gives a quotient of 18 with a remainder of 6, so 6 cards are left over.

bank.question: After 144 study cards are arranged into equal groups of 8, how many cards are left over?
bank.explanation: Dividing 144 by 8 gives a quotient of 18 with a remainder of 0, so 0 cards are left over.

bank.question: During a GMAT preparation review for the Alpha cohort, case note 001 says a training provider surveyed only people who had already paid for advanced support and found that most reported a high attendance level. The director concludes that all prospective students would value the same support. Which option most weakens the director's conclusion?
bank.explanation: The conclusion moves from a self-selected paying group to all prospective students. Showing that the surveyed group is not representative weakens that move.
options: Some respondents used the support more than once.
The surveyed group had already shown unusual interest in the support being assessed.
The director has worked in admissions for several years.
The survey was completed online rather than on paper.

bank.question: In a recent admissions report for the Orchard cohort, case note 003 says an executive programme plans to shorten each practice review because candidates often stop reading long feedback notes. The team expects shorter reviews to improve the attendance level. Which assumption is required?
bank.explanation: The plan depends on shorter feedback remaining useful. If it becomes too vague, reading more of it would not necessarily improve performance.
options: Candidates prefer printed notes to digital notes.
Every candidate has the same target score.
Shorter reviews will still contain enough specific guidance for candidates to act on.
The team will reduce the number of practice questions.

bank.question: Following a pilot programme for the Dover cohort, case note 005 says an entrepreneurship hub will fund either additional mock tests or additional feedback sessions, but not both. It will choose feedback sessions unless fewer than half of candidates submit practice essays. This week, more than half submitted practice essays. Which conclusion follows?
bank.explanation: The rule says feedback is chosen unless the submission condition falls below half. Since more than half submitted, the exception does not apply.
options: The mock tests are less expensive than feedback sessions.
The candidates who submitted essays all need feedback.
The organisation will choose additional feedback sessions rather than additional mock tests.
The organisation will fund both options.

bank.question: Analysing candidate data for the Harbour cohort, case note 002 says a student society introduced weekly analytics drills, and its candidates then achieved a higher response time. The manager claims the drills caused the improvement. Which finding would most strengthen the claim?
bank.explanation: If the new cohort started from a similar level, the later improvement is more plausibly linked to the drills rather than to an already stronger group.
options: The drills were popular with candidates who already liked analytics.
The candidates had similar prior results to earlier cohorts before the drills began.
The manager also redesigned the office noticeboard that month.
The candidates took the exam on different weekdays.

bank.question: Near the end of reading the following passage about data literacy, answer the question. Many managers can read a chart but still draw poor conclusions from it. Data literacy requires attention to the source, the scale, the units and the question being asked. A rising line may look impressive, but it matters whether the starting point was unusually low or whether a small sample produced the pattern. Good analysts therefore combine calculation with scepticism about context. Which option best describes the role of the final sentence in the passage?
bank.explanation: The author stresses scale, source, sample and context alongside calculation, so the best summary combines numerical skill with contextual caution.
options: The passage argues that sample size is irrelevant when the trend is clear.
The passage says charts are usually less reliable than written summaries.
The passage emphasises that interpreting data well requires both numerical skill and attention to context.
The passage claims that rising lines always indicate strong performance.

bank.question: Reviewing study outcomes for the Vista cohort, case note 004 says applicants who attend optional strategy sessions tend to have stronger response time. A tutor concludes that attending the sessions is the main reason for the stronger results. Which option identifies the main flaw?
bank.explanation: The reasoning treats correlation as causation without ruling out motivation as a common cause of both attendance and performance.
options: The argument overlooks that more motivated applicants may be more likely both to attend and to perform well.
The sessions are optional rather than compulsory.
The tutor does not state the exact room used for the sessions.
The argument compares applicants from different countries.

bank.question: As part of reading the following passage about time management, answer the question. Timed practice can reveal habits that untimed study hides. Some candidates spend too long on questions they are unlikely to solve, while others rush through questions they could answer correctly with another minute of thought. Reviewing timing data after practice can therefore be as valuable as reviewing accuracy alone. The aim is not to make every question equally fast but to allocate effort where it is most likely to improve the final score. Which inference is best supported by the passage?
bank.explanation: The passage says timing review reveals habits and helps candidates allocate effort where it is most likely to improve the final score.
options: The passage says every GMAT question should receive exactly the same amount of time.
The passage states that rushing is always better than persistence.
The passage recommends ignoring accuracy after a timed test.
The passage argues that timing data helps candidates decide where their effort is most productively spent.

bank.question: Within reading the following passage about business school selection, answer the question. Business schools often use admissions tests alongside essays, references and interviews. The purpose is not to reduce applicants to a single number but to add a comparable measure to a broader file. A high score may show readiness for demanding coursework, yet it cannot by itself demonstrate leadership, judgement or fit with a programme. Admissions teams therefore treat the test as one structured input among several. Which statement most accurately captures the author's view?
bank.explanation: The passage describes the test as one structured input and says it cannot by itself show qualities such as leadership or fit.
options: The passage says essays are irrelevant once a test score is available.
The passage states that interviews should always be removed from selection.
The passage suggests that admissions tests are useful because they provide a comparable measure, but they do not replace broader judgement.
The passage argues that leadership can be measured only by a GMAT score.

bank.question: Near the end of a data sufficiency review for a campus consultancy club, the target value is x. Is x uniquely determined? Statement 1: x plus y equals 19. Statement 2: x minus y equals -1.
bank.explanation: Statement 1 alone allows several x and y pairs, and statement 2 alone also allows several pairs. Together, the two equations determine x uniquely, so both together are sufficient but neither alone is sufficient.
options: Statement 1 alone is sufficient, but statement 2 alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Each statement alone is sufficient.
Statement 2 alone is sufficient, but statement 1 alone is not sufficient.

bank.question: Across reading the following passage about adaptive practice, answer the question. A student who misses a percentage problem because of a reading mistake needs a different follow-up from one who misunderstands the arithmetic. options: The sessions were held in the same building as before.
The remaining emails were personalised and sent only to candidates whose chosen topics matched the session.
The organisation also bought new chairs.
The email font was slightly smaller than usual.

bank.question: Late in a mock-test cycle for the Cobalt cohort, case note 010 says a case workshop claims its new question review tool is better than its old one because users made fewer repeated mistakes. Which evidence best supports the claim?
bank.explanation: A fair comparison needs similar users and similar tasks. That makes the lower repeat-error rate more attributable to the new tool.
options: The old tool was available for several years.
The same types of users attempted comparable question sets before and after the tool changed.
The new tool has a different logo.
Some users reviewed questions at weekends.

options: The organisation published its timetable in advance.
The course had a shorter name than the previous one.
A small number of very high-scoring candidates joined the course and lifted the average sharply.
Some candidates completed the course on tablets.

bank.question: Applicant feedback from the programme for the Kensington cohort, case note 006 says a prep platform wants to raise the response time by replacing live workshops with recorded lessons. Which question would be most useful in evaluating the plan?

options: Were the recorded lessons filmed in the morning?
Do candidates currently benefit more from asking questions during live workshops than from replaying material?
How many staff members use the same meeting room?
What colour are the slides used in the lessons?
